recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if OO decides to reopen the normative-compatible Group indirection model or to define a new cross-resource Observation search parameter for member specimens; FHIR-34002 itself is already applied correctly.
issue_request: FHIR-34002 was a Published / Persuasive with Modification R4 issue asking how a single Observation can identify multiple specimens without changing normative Observation.specimen from 0..1 to 0..*. The approved path was to allow Observation.specimen to reference a Group, constrain that Group to specimens, and account for searching through Group member behavior.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied for R5 in fd8f971f11 / PR #2178 by adding Group as a targetProfile on Observation.specimen and adding invariant obs-9. Later invariant QA commits 55512f8e09, 9b24283fc, and a82569d3be refined obs-9 into the current expression. The related FHIR-35972 application in 7816ce8037 added Specimen to Group.member.entity.
additional_context: OO minutes from 2022-03-07 confirm the rationale: keep one Observation.specimen reference, allow either one Specimen or a Group of specimens, place the invariant on Observation.specimen, and rely on Group.member search after Specimen is added to Group.member.entity. Later decisions reinforce rather than reverse the model: FHIR-38732 added grouping guidance, FHIR-39269 retained Specimen in Group to avoid breaking Observation, and FHIR-54865 was retracted.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. source/fhir.ini keeps Observation, Group, and Specimen active; Observation.specimen is 0..1 Reference(Specimen|Group) with obs-9; Group includes Specimen as a type and member target; Group.member has a reference search parameter; and the Specimen notes describe grouping through Observation.specimen.

related_jiras.note: Added Specimen to Group.member.entity so a specimen-only Group can support the FHIR-34002 Observation model.
Added Specimen grouping guidance that explicitly mentions grouping at Observation.specimen.
Retained Specimen in Group and added rationale because removing it would break the Observation multiple-specimen model.
A later R6 challenge to Observation.specimen Reference(Group) was retracted, leaving the FHIR-34002 model intact.
